mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for two consecutive months reduces near-term discounting of corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or flat despite sustained high FEDFUNDS, with p-value > 0.05 in a backtest.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in hourly wage growth (indirect via UNRATE) weakens consumer demand, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses above 150,000 while UNRATE falls below 4.0%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite rising PAYEMS and falling UNRATE, with statistical significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average signals accelerating economic momentum, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns underperform a 5-day moving average baseline with p-value < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained double-digit decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 3% for three consecutive months reduces policy uncertainty, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls below 3.0% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant return advantage over 20 days when CPIAUCSL remains volatile or spikes unexpectedly.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the 10-year yield proxy (assumed via FEDFUNDS behavior) combined with elevated retail employment (PAYEMS) creates a dual signal of rate cut anticipation and strong labor market, producing positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS falls by > 0.25% in a single month while PAYEMS exceeds 145,000
failure_condition: Forward returns underperform a no-rate-cut baseline with p-value > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment (PAYEMS) without a corresponding drop in wage rates (UNRATE) indicates labor market stress, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses above 160,000 while UNRATE stays above 4.2%
regime_hint: labor market weakening without wage suppression
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite repeated PAYEMS spikes and flat UNRATE.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail sales proxies (assumed via HOUST) above trend suggest consumer confidence is improving, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant improvement over a 30-day baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month average triggers supply-side risk, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive during multiple INDPRO contractions with high Sharpe ratio.
